# dsh-task-gantt
**An agent-team task Gantt chart for the DeepSeek Harness sidebar** — one swimlane per teammate on t
he y-axis, real session time on the x-axis, and every shared task drawn with its title and summary.
English | 中文

nt agent colours, tasks of clearly different durations,
> one still running, message arrows in both

directions), captured from a real
> browser at 2× and cropped to the panel itself: `docs/screenshots

/panel-v4.png`.
> It is labelled as such on purpose: the drawing is the shipped component, but the
>

DATA is a fixture, so it is not a real-team capture. The footer in the image
> carries the build id

entity (`v0.2.11 · label-in-box`), which is how a reader can

ning shots (board overview from real team data, task-card detail,

g; see

`dsh-task-gantt` is a plugin for dsh-better-sidebar: it registers one extra sidebar tab. It is **rea
d-only** — it never creates, claims, or completes a task.
## Project status

| Version | `0.3.3` |
| Frozen contract (`src/shared/contract.ts`) | done |
| Host data layer (`src/

host/**`) | in progress |
| Sidebar tab registration (`src/client/index.ts`) | done |
| Gantt render

ing (`src/client/ui/**`) | in progress |
| Real-machine mount smoke test | not run yet |

The chart is described below **as specified by the frozen contract**; for what has
actually been exe

cuted and observed, read
`docs/VALIDATION.md` (owned by the verification teammate) —
this README doe
s not restate untested claims as results.
## What you get

- **Swimlanes = the roster.** The Lead first, then the teammates in roster order,
then an `unassigne

d` row for tasks the board has not handed to anyone.
- **A real time axis.** Every span and every ta

sk transition is dated from the
durable session event log (epoch ms) — not from "when the panel happ

ened to
open".
- **Turn bands with step bars inside.** A whole prompt/response turn is a faint
band;

each model step inside it is a solid bar. A span that has not closed yet
is drawn open-ended and ex

tends toward now.
- **Task chips carry the work, not just a colour.** `subject` plus a one-line
`des

cription`, with status, owner, `blockedBy`, `writeScopes` and readiness in
the detail view.
- **Hone

st degradation.** When a lane cannot be dated, the panel says so and
labels the task as live instead

of inventing an interval.
- **Themed by tokens, bilingual by default.** All colour comes from DSH's

`--dsw-alias-*` / `--dsw-font-*` / `--ds-*` tokens, so every skin works; the UI
is Chinese or Engli
sh depending on the page language.

The plugin declares one peer, `@deepseek-ai/cordis@^4.0.0`, and marks it
optional. It declares **no*

* `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer on purpose: the host's
startup compatibility preflight evaluates those r

anges and silently disables the
whole profile row when one fails. See `docs/DESIGN.md` §8.

If `dsh-better-sidebar` is not installed, the plugin still loads and logs one
warning; it simply has
no tab to register into.

## How it works

The chart is assembled from **two** sources, because either one alone cannot draw
it:

1. **The `agentTeam` session projection** (browser side) is authoritative for
*what exists and what

state it is in* — the roster, phases, and the shared
tasks with their status, owner, dependencies an

d write scopes. **It contains no
timestamps at all**: neither the member records nor the task record

s carry a
`createdAt` / `startedAt` / `completedAt`. It can tell you a task is
`completed`; it can n

ever tell you *when*.
2. **The durable session event log** (host side, one log per session — the Lea

d
and each teammate) is the only authoritative clock. Events carry `time` (epoch
ms) and `seq`. The

host half reads the logs and folds them into activity spans
and dated task transitions.

The host half exposes the folded result over a small read-only JSON API
(`POST /dsh-task-gantt/api/t

imeline`), and the browser half renders it. The
browser cannot read session logs itself, which is wh

browser half renders it. The
browser cannot read session logs itself, which is why the split exists.
